content:
Good morning, Stacy.

You should never have to open a message to move it or delete it. Some people have reported that a Thunderbird update changed their view from table view to cards view. Maybe that's what happened to you and why you saw few messages instead of a long list. Please see the attached screenpic. If you click on the icon that is circled in red, is there a check mark next to "Table View" or "Cards View". If it is next to "Cards View", you may want to select "Table View" instead.

It will be easy to move all your old messages at one time as long as you have them in local folders. After that, all that is needed is to copy those folders to your external drive, then copy them to the right location on your laptop computer.

  1. Put all the messages that you want to keep in local folders.
  2. Use "Help" menu > Troubleshooting information > about:profiles, find your active profiles, and select the option for showing its root directory.
  3. Drill down to mail/local folders.
  4. Copy all the files without the .msf extension to your external drive.
  5. On your laptop, reverse the operation: close Thunderbird, copy all those files to mail/local folders in your active profile, open Thunderbird.

This operation may be a bit complex for you. When you are ready, you may want to start a new discussion in this forum and ask for help with just that operation.

Moving "recipients" is another matter. Apparently, you want to move your address book(s) to your laptop computer. I am not familiar with address books in Windows. You may want to start a new discussion for that process too.

content:
re : I am finding that dozens of folders I have deleted reappear in the Thunderbird folder list as italicized,

Folders that are grey and use italics have a 'no-select' flag which means they cannot contain emails themselves but can contain folders that do contain emails.

I can offer some info on how Gmail can show an italicized folder, so it might help explain things so you can check the ms server.

In Gmail Settings > Labels

In the section where you create your own labels/folders The top level says [Gmail]/ - if this was allowed to display in Folder Pane it would be italicized as it has that / to denote it is a no-select folder.

It contains some folders I created: INBOX/Mozilla Firefox - in Thunderbird Folder pane, 'Mozilla Firefox' displays as a sub folder to Inbox and neither are italicized. Oldstore - in Thunderbird Folder pane, 'Oldstore' displays as a top level folder in mail account and is not italicized.

But I wanted an italicized folder called 'Testing', so I created a folder which has a / after it: Testing/ - in Thunderbird Folder pane, 'Testing' displays as a top level folder in mail account and it is italicized. I wanted that 'Testing' folder to contain a sub folder called 'Sub Test' so I then created: Testing/Sub Test - in Thunderbird Folder pane, 'Sub Test' displays as a sub folder to Testing. Only Testing is italicized - Sub Test is not italicized.

See the two images I posted below. Once shows the above info in Gmail and the other shows the Folder Pane view - I also included the 'Subscribe' list.

Please notice in 'Subscribe' list - I did not select to see the italicized 'Testing' folder, but I did select to see the 'Sub Test' folder. If I unsubscribe from seeing 'Sub Test' it does not remove the 'Testing' italicised folder. To force the italicized to disappear - in gmail I edit the name by removing the /, so it's now just plain 'Testing' not 'Testing/' Then I can delete it or not subscribe to see it etc.

This info explains how I can create no-select folders in gmail - maybe this may help you to work out what is displayed in 365 server.
